recipes.name: Best Ever Jalapeño Poppers
ingredients_raw: 12 ounces jalapeño peppers, seeded and halved
2 quarts oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Mix cream cheese, Cheddar cheese, and bacon bits together in a medium bowl until well combined. Spoon mixture into jalapeño halves.
Put milk in one small bowl, flour in a second, and bread crumbs in a third.
Dip stuffed jalapeños in milk, then in flour, making sure they are well-coated. Transfer coated jalapeños to a plate; let dry for 10 minutes.

Dip jalapeños in milk once more, then roll through the bread crumbs. Let dry on the plate for 10 minutes, then repeat dipping in milk and rolling in bread crumbs once more; make sure they are completely coated. Let dry.
Heat oil to 365 degrees F (180 degrees C) in a medium skillet.
Working in batches if necessary, deep-fry coated jalapeños until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove and let drain on a paper towel.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Ever Jalapeño Poppers
raw_recipe.description: Homemade jalapeño poppers full of gooey cheese and savory bacon bits are deep fried to golden perfections. These party poppers are hard to resist!

video.description: The homemade jalapeño poppers recipe in this video was made by taking the best features of three or four other popper recipes and combining them to make something that tastes wonderful.
video.name: How to Make the Best Ever Jalapeño Poppers

review.reviewBody: I used monteray jack cheese and reduced fat cream cheese. Only coated them twice. Made 100 and put them in the freezer. I bake mine at 350 until cheese is hot and bubbly.........mmmmmmm....yummy!! I prefer baked not fried.

I see many negative reviews about the peppers that are not hot (spicy). That's your own fault. Supermarket Jalapeños are rarely spicy, grow your own (I suggest Biker Billy Hybrids). As far as the filling being bland, yes cream cheese with a minimal amount of bacon bits and cheddar would be pretty bland. Use chopped fresh cooked bacon, browned hot or sweet italian sausage and a very sharp cheddar with some parmesan (or romano cheese) added and your complaints will disappear. The breading technique is invaluable, but you could also spice up the breading mix with 'your choice' of a Chili Powder (ancho, cayenne, hot or sweet paprika, etc.) to spice it up. Don't be shy about experimenting, everyone has their own taste preferences and spice tolerance. The blanching technique as suggested in the comments will give you a softer pepper to fry.

These were Epicly Delicious! After reading many reviews I made some tweeks: I oven Roasted the Jalepenos whole for 25 mins @ 400°F. Then I de-seeded them and chopped all the pulp and seeds and added them to the Cream Cheese- Cheddar mix for some heat and extra flavor. I used 16oz of Cream Cheese instead of 12 for a bigger batch. I added Salt, Garlic Powder, and Onion powder to the Cheese. I also seasoned the Breadcrumbs with Salt, Pepper, Cayenne, Garlic Powder, Onion Powder, and Italian Herbs. I double breaded the poppers by dipping them a 2nd time in the Breadcrumbs, as recommended. I also used Oatmilk cause that is all I had, but next time will use Eggs instead of milk to make the batter stick more evenly. I recommended using a cooking Themometer to make sure your oil is not too hot, but not too cool. If it's too hot, it effects the flavor. If it's too cool, the batter may come off in some places. I will use one next batch I make to accelerate the process and make them all come out consistent. Overall, they were epic though! My family loved them and chowed them down with rave reviews. Next time I might just chop up all the oven roasted jalapeños and all them to the cheese mix and form them into log-shapes and bread and fry them that way for a faster process. Maybe also try some in the airfryer. Highly recommend this recipe as the foundation though. Happy Cooking Adventures!

I, like many others have augmented this recipe. I blanched the whole peppers, cooled in an ice bath, sliced off the tops, halved and cleaned them. I used a cream cheese and shredded cheddar jack cheese mixture. I placed them in the freezer just long enough to firm the cheese. I proceeded with the milk and flour twice and milk and bread crumbs twice. Let them rest well between each coating! They should look as though they were battered after 8-10 minutes. Season your crumbs heavily. I used dried chives and chili powder...try anything. I fried in veg shortening. EXCELLENT! Cripsy without cheese loss. Wear gloves when cleaning the peppers and do not place frozen peppers in hot oil! This is laborious but well worth it.

I made these poppers for Kentucky Derby party and they were a big hit. However, I modified a few things and learned a few things and want to share with you. (1) Equal parts Extra Sharp Cheddar Cheese, Pepper Jack, and cream cheese. (2) Cooked 1 lb. of bacon, diced and added to cheese mixture for 50 poppers. (3) Mound cheese above pepper... lots of cheese. (4) Although I coated three times with milk-dry ingredient bath, the dry ingredient was different each time... (1st) milk and all purpose flour (2nd) milk and Panko bread crumbs (3rd) I use this coating for my fried green tomatoes... milk and dry: 2 parts dry, finely grated parmesan cheese and 1 part corn meal. Make sure each coating is dry before adding next coating. I deep fried four-at-a- time in approx. 4 inches of hot Canola Oil for approx. 3 - 4 minutes max. and turned them in the oil constantly. They were delicious!!!! And by the way, believe it or not, they paired perfectly with the Mint Julips (which were delicious too!!!). The worst part of the day: my horse didn't win.

Like several people I used this recipe as a jumping off place; I modified it to fit my tastes and dietary guidelines. I’m a type 2 diabetic and follow ketogenic a diet so I skipped the milk bath, flour and breadcrumbs. 
I doubled the amount of bacon, using real bacon, with an equal quantity of chopped pepperoni. Equal portions of onion powder and garlic powder raised the flavor level. I cut off both ends of the peppers and blanched for 2 minutes in boiling water. This made them easier to remove the insides and milder. Instead of halving them I laid them flat on the cutting board and split one side. After removing the seeds with the back of my cutting knife I spooned in the cheese mixture and folded them closed against themselves. 
Lastly, I used the baking sheet I used to bake the bacon with melted residual bacon fat on it and baked them in the oven instead of deep frying.

OK, this recipe was a good starting point, but I tweaked it a bit, and the results were a hit at my recent party. 1) I blanched the seeded, halved peppers (2 mins in boiling water, cooling in ice water). 2) I reserved a handful of the blanched peppers to add to the filling. I also added white and green onions, red bell pepper, fresh garlic, chili powder, cumin, salt, and freshly ground black pepper, and upped the amount of bacon (I used real bacon ends and pieces I keep frozen for just such recipes). After cooking the bacon pieces, I added the filling ingredients plus all my extras above to the bowl of my food processor and blended until it was a rough mixture. 3) I filled the drained, dried pepper halves as per the recipe, but I made sure that the filling was heaped on top (probably double the amount--trust me, it will cook down). Then, I froze the filled halves on cookie sheets until solid. 4) I did the milk and flour coating per the recipe, but added salt and chili powder to the flour after a test fry revealed that the breading was pasty and bland. When it came time for the second coating, I used panko. 5) I cooked the still mostly frozen peppers in my deep fryer at 365 for about 2 minutes. PERFECTION!!!

I blanched the peppers first. I added Adobo seasoning to the cheese mixture and a sprinkle to the panko, some chopped cilantro and doubled the bacon bits. I fried half the batch and baked half in 400° for 30 minutes. The fried batch took 90 minutes to table and the baked batch took 2 hours to table. The baked ones were less messy and had the same crunch and flavor without all the oil (fried on left, baked on right)

I thought these were a little bland, but they were well-received at my party. I followed the recipe, but added more bacon pieces after tasting the filling. Even so, I still couldn't taste the bacon in the finished product. I used panko bread crumbs for extra crunch. I only rolled them in the bread crumbs once, as I ran out of time. I couldn't bring myself to fry them, so I baked them at 350 degrees for 30 minutes. Reduced fat cream cheese or neufchatel works well in this recipe.

5 Star With Tweaks. New review. Prep Time is still a LOT longer than 25 minutes. For a few peppers plan on at least an hour. Absolutely par boil or roast (i roasted until they were soft but firm) the jalapenos before filling. It made ALL the difference in texture and flavor; as written the peppers are just raw. Had to tweak the breadcrumb mix because I ran out of bread crumbs, and added salt and onion powder to the cheese. Hands down, with tweaks, this is now a favorite.

Giving 5 stars even though I swapped out the bacon for green scallions. I par-boiled the peppers to aid in softening. When ppl say wear gloves...please wear gloves. My poor fingers are still burning hours later. But, my goodness, these things are awesome. Due to diet issues, I also used gluten free seasoned bread crumbs. After the 3rd drudge in milk and second crumb coating, it was next to impossible to know what side was cheese. I used my air fryer at 395 degrees 5 minutes one side and 4 minutes on second. Perfect! These will be made again for sure. Makes enough to freeze and reheat what you want for later, or for a group/party.

I actually used a super sharp vegetable peeler and peeled the raw jalapenos. I thought about roasting them that I didn't want them to get over cooked. I also added some lawrys crispy chicken mix to the bread crumbs! So amazing. I made them two days in a row.

I followed this fairly close, however used a Mexican cheese mix (Cheddar, Jack, Asadero, Chihuahua) in place of Cheddar, and Panko instead of standard breadcrumbs. The whole family agreed that they are the best we have had.

This worked well for me. Primarily, I wanted to test a cheese/filling idea, I'm working toward a recipe for Malawe Picante / Peppadew poppers, when my plants produce a crop sometime aroundlate July or August. The filling I tried was 8 oz of cream cheese with 6 oz of Merlot infused (cheddar/parm ?) from BellaVitano. No bacon (or any meat) in the filling, but I did add 1 diced jalapeno to half of the filling. Other changes: Buttermilk subbed for whole milk, 1 egg in the 2 cups buttermilk for the wash. Panko breadcrumbs mixed 50/50 with corn flake crumbs. I double dredged half, and gave the other half a third dredge and panko/cornflake coating. Also, half the peppers were jalapeno, the other half were mini sweet horn shaped. The jalapenos lacked heat and flavor, and tasted a bit green - I blame underripe picking at far distant farms for February delivery to Ohio. (Nod to Ray Hines' comment here from 2023..) (Peppers will ripen after picking, but it is known that they stop developing heat and flavor..). The sweet peppers were quite underwhelming - same attribution of cause. It's OK.. my target pepper is the Malawe Piquante (a.k.a. Pepperdew), which has a distinctive fruity-sweet flavor and just a whisper of Scoville heat (maybe 1000 - 1500 SHU..). Also, I was in a hurry, so I did not freeze the peppers after breading them.. so the cheese started to melt earlier, and the peppers didn't get fully cooked. But.. the cheese filling was fantastic, and I think it'll work very well with the intended pepper.
Filling was great, also enjoyed the heat level just enough. Jalapeños little hard. Might try blanching or roasting them first!

Was buying the cardboard boxed brand but my son could wipe those out on his own. These however give flavor that are worth the effort (and cheaper for the quantity) I parboiled the unseeded peppers. The first time I made they were not tender enough for me. Lots of cheese and bacon please with a shake of garlic! So nice to be able to customize to your taste. Oh and these reheat in air fryer great.

Great recipe! I forgot bacon bits and cheedar and it was still delicious! Made my own breadcrumbs with toasted bread using a cheese grater, man I love Allrecipes! I'm new to the app and wish I had found it years ago! Thanks for sharing!
Very easy to make, they taste awesome!
The whole family loved these. Will definitely make them again. Just wondering if it's possible to make these and freeze them before cooking??
Great recipe 👌
